text.p: Ford Motor Co said Wednesday it is recalling 27,553 Expedition full-size sport utilities in the U.S. and Canada because of problems with suspension weld attachments.

Ford said the weld between the track bar bracket and frame crossmember may not attach sufficiently. A small number of vehicles may also not have a strong enough weld attachment between the left hand lower control arm and rear axle housing.
If both welds were to break, the rear frame and body could move sideways and affect vehicle control. If one of the welds separate, drivers may experience a sway during lane changes.
About 1,639 of the recalled vehicles are in Canada. It is the first recall of the popular sport/utility vehicle, which officially went on sale in September 1996.

Since production began, Ford has made 110,000 of the vehicles through today. The vehicles included in the recall were made between March 1 and October 10 of 1996. Expeditions are made at Ford's Michigan Truck plant in Wayne, Mich.
Ford spokeswoman Karen Shaughnessy said no accidents or injuries have been reported as result of the problems.
